discovery: Development of silicon microstrip and pixel detectors for precision tracking and vertexing of particles

nominees.name: Josef Kemmer
nominees.affiliation: Technical University of Munich / PNSensor, Germany

subfield: Particle detector instrumentation / experimental particle physics
motivation: Silicon detectors transformed how we see particles. Kemmer's 1980 adaptation of the planar process to silicon sensors made low-noise, finely segmented microstrip detectors practical. Heijne pioneered silicon microstrip and then hybrid pixel detectors with integrated readout electronics at CERN, leading to the pixel trackers at the core of every LHC experiment and to Medipix imaging. Parker conceived monolithic and 3D-electrode silicon sensors, radiation-hard designs now installed in ATLAS and CMS. Together these inventions gave micron-scale vertex resolution, which enabled heavy-flavour tagging. That tagging was essential to the top-quark discovery at the Tevatron, to precision B physics and CP violation, and to observing Higgs decays to b-quarks. Beyond particle physics, the technology underpins X-ray imaging, synchrotron science, astrophysics and medical diagnostics. Few instruments have made so many measurements possible that were impossible before.
